text.p: Lindsay Manufacturing Co said Wednesday favorable market factors and corresponding strong demand for irrigation equipment resulted in increased backlog.
As of August 31, order backlog totaled $25.7 million, up 77 percent from last year's order backlog of $14.5 million.
"Continued strength in the North American agriculture sector should favorably affect Lindsay's top-line growth through fiscal 1997," Gary Parker, chairman, said in a statement.

"As farmers' confidence rises along with their income, we expect to see them increase their capital investment and, with the ability to lower irrigation related variable production costs by as much as 25 percent, center pivot irrigation equipment should be high on many farmers' priority lists," Parker added.
Lindsay said its North American irrigation equipment revenues in fiscal 1996 grew by 25 percent, with export irrigation equipment sales rising 79 percent over fiscal 1995.

Stronger irrigation equipment revenue more than offset an expected decline in fiscal 1996 diversified products revenue. That drop was caused by weaker demand for Lindsay's large diameter steel tubing used by grain handling equipment manufacturers, as U.S. grain reserves hit near record lows.
Revenues from diversified products were down 12 percent in fiscal 1996, totaling $20.3 million compared with $23.0 million in fiscal 1995.
Earlier, Lindsay reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.37 a share, up from $0.27 a year ago. For fiscal 1996, it earned $2.44 a share, up from $1.65.
